page: Microsoft Azure D48s_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DSv3 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 48 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per virtual core.

This server includes 393 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage configurations. It does not feature any GPU acceleration, relying entirely on the host CPU for computational tasks. The underlying virtualization is managed via Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance tradeoff. Single-core performance is categorized as weak, falling into the bottom 25% across multiple tests, including stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded compression. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by multi-threaded Geekbench, PassMark, and stress-ng results. Memory bandwidth and database operations, such as Redis SET commands, also perform in the average tier. Consequently, this server is suited for multi-threaded workloads, general-purpose web serving, and database operations that can leverage the high core count, rather than single-threaded or large-scale LLM inference tasks.
